goal.title: Count how widely the exception spreads
goal.concept: A field's cardinality is how many distinct values it takes. One distinct value means every record shares it; many mean it spreads.
goal.narration: Switch from Documents to Field statistics, and read the Distinct values column for these records. How many services, and how many separate requests, do they come from?
goal.reasoning: Counting distinct values shows whether the exception comes from only one service. It also shows whether it hit one request again and again, or many separate requests.
goal.evidence: Field statistics count each field's distinct values among the records in view.

demonstration.narration: I'll switch to Field statistics and count the distinct values of service.name and trace.id among these records.
demonstration.reasoning: Cardinality is the number of distinct values a field has. It shows how far something spreads. One service means the exception happens only there. Many trace IDs mean it hit many separate requests, not one request retried.
demonstration.evidence: service.name has 1 distinct value: every record that raised the exception comes from ${param.incident.service}. trace.id has several, so it struck several separate requests, not one request retried.

goal.title: See what happened just before the exception
goal.concept: Surrounding documents list the events logged just before and after one event, whatever the search was. So you can see what led up to it.
goal.narration: In the event you opened, find the Actions at the top of the document and choose View surrounding documents. Then open the event logged just before it.
goal.reasoning: A filter shows the exception on its own. The events logged around it show what the same request did just before it failed.
goal.evidence: The event just before the exception belongs to the same request and shows what happened first.
